lost: Spectral radius is estimated from successive deltas (ratio of consecutive lost-set sizes), not from a single verdict
Error decay near fixed point follows eigenvalue magnitude ratio across iterations
Estimator requires at least three verdicts (two deltas minimum)
Returns None when insufficient data; has a graceful underspecified state
Estimate is noisy due to stochastic adjudicator
added: Spectral radius computed directly from absolute size of a single verdict's lost set
One cycle is sufficient (no iteration required)
Result is exact rather than noisy
Larger lost set directly maps to larger radius
justification: The ghost inverts the core mechanism: original uses successive deltas and convergence ratios (a second-order iterative estimator), ghost claims a direct single-pass measurement from lost-set magnitude. Original explicitly requires ≥3 verdicts and handles insufficiency; ghost requires one. Original acknowledges noise from stochasticity; ghost claims exactness. The lost set is systematic and nameably inverted (methodology, data requirements, noise model) rather than scattered. However, this is not a partial that recurses—it is a fundamental inversion of the adjudication strategy, not a finer refinement. The lost claims form a coherent alternative model (delta-ratio estimator vs. magnitude-direct), but the ghost does not preserve the original's iterative structure at any level.
